questions.ideal_answer: RDB snapshotting and hybrid persistence differ in several ways: RDB snapshotting is point-in-time backup (works by fork-based persistence) whereas hybrid persistence is RDB + AOF combined (works by Redis 4.0+ feature). questions.question: Explain the difference between pipelining and Lua scripting in Redis.
questions.ideal_answer: pipelining and Lua scripting differ in several ways: pipelining is batch command execution (works by reducing RTT overhead) whereas Lua scripting is server-side execution (works by atomic multi-command operations). pipelining is typically used for sending multiple commands without waiting for responses, while Lua scripting is used for EVAL, EVALSHA, script load. Example demonstrating pipelining: pipeline = r.pipeline(); pipeline.get('a'); pipeline.set('b', 2); pipeline.execute(). Example demonstrating Lua scripting: EVAL 'return redis.call("get", KEYS[1]) + redis.call("get", KEYS[2])' 2 key1 key2.

questions.question: Explain the difference between write-through and eviction policies in Redis.
questions.ideal_answer: write-through and eviction policies differ in several ways: write-through is synchronous write pattern (works by cache and DB updated together) whereas eviction policies is memory full handling (works by determining which keys to remove). write-through is typically used for write to cache and DB simultaneously, while eviction policies is used for noeviction, allkeys-lru, volatile-lru, allkeys-random, volatile-ttl. Example demonstrating write-through: cache.set(key, value); db.write(key, value). Example demonstrating eviction policies: maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru.
